name: Glomus Tumors of Head and Neck

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiologic Diagnostic Criteria for Head and Neck Paragangliomas

criteria.description: Identification of highly vascular mass on imaging (MRI/CT) in typical locations (temporal bone, carotid body)
Presence of pulsatile tinnitus, hearing loss, or neck mass consistent with tumor location
Histological confirmation showing chief cells and sustentacular cells with characteristic Zellballen pattern
Elevated plasma or urine catecholamines or metanephrines (in functional tumors)
Positive family history or genetic mutation associated with paragangliomas (e.g. SDH mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic vascular mass on imaging plus clinical presentation consistent with tumor location; histopathological confirmation if biopsy performed
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Biopsy is often avoided due to vascularity; diagnosis frequently based on imaging and clinical features.

occasional.symptomName: Cranial nerve palsies (e.g. IX, X, XI, XII)
occasional.notes: May cause dysphonia, dysphagia, shoulder weakness

laboratory: Elevated plasma or urine catecholamines/metanephrines in functional tumors
imaging: MRI showing highly vascular mass with 'salt and pepper' appearance
CT demonstrating enhancing mass at carotid bifurcation or temporal bone
Digital subtraction angiography showing tumor vascularity and feeding vessels
genetic: Mutations in SDH gene complex (SDHB, SDHD, SDHC) associated with familial cases
other: Histopathology showing Zellballen pattern with chief and sustentacular cells
Positive uptake on 123I-MIBG or 68Ga-DOTATATE PET scans

distinguishingFeatures: Pulsatile mass but with vascular lumen continuity
Absence of tumor cells on imaging

redFlags: Severe hypertension in context of functional tumor
references: Lloyd RV, Osamura RY, Klöppel G, Rosai J. WHO Classification of Tumours of Endocrine Organs. 4th ed. IARC; 2017.
Mendenhall WM, Amdur RJ, Morris CG. Paragangliomas of the head and neck. Am J Clin Oncol. 2005;28(3):234-239.
Neumann HP, Bausch B, McWhinney SR, et al. Germ-line mutations in nonsyndromic pheochromocytoma. N Engl J Med. 2002;346(19):1459-1466.
